subject.original: Current ORMA paw-protection guide reviewed from the repository.

result.title: Make the paw-check advice easier to act on
result.summary: Two small edits turn general advice into a clearer trail routine while preserving the guide's existing scope and cautious tone.

changes.before: • Check pads at rest stops. Look for redness, cuts, or unusual sensitivity before continuing.
changes.after: • Check every paw at rest stops, including between the toes. Pause before continuing if you notice redness, a cut, debris, or unusual sensitivity.
changes.reason: Makes the existing check more specific without adding a diagnosis or treatment claim.

changes.before: • Consider trail booties for any route tagged with scree or sharp-rock hazards, especially on longer distances.
changes.after: • Consider trail booties for routes tagged with scree or sharp-rock hazards, especially over longer distances. Test the fit on a short walk before relying on them for a full day.
changes.reason: Adds a practical preparation step and avoids implying that unfamiliar equipment should first be used on a long mountain route.

sources.label: American Veterinary Medical Association · pet first aid
sources.supports: Inspecting an affected paw and seeking veterinary care when an injury is suspected.
